endToEnd.notes: End-to-end landed cost from factory to consumer. FOB is computed per source country from the actual labour and machine rates in assumptions.locations. Matrix is derived from tradeRules and updated live by the tariff simulator. Carbon cost added for EU destinations per carbonRules.

tradeRules.notes: Rules to compute the landed-cost matrix live. Adding a source country needs only a matching location in assumptions.locations with the same id.

carbonRules.notes: EU ETS price ~€85/tCO2e (Q4 2026 forecast). CBAM currently covers cement, iron/steel, aluminium, fertilisers, electricity, hydrogen — footwear is not yet in scope. Modelled here as an indicative scope-3 pass-through cost to EU destinations.

processFlow.notes: The end-to-end shoe manufacturing journey. Cost shares are typical percentages of FOB for a running shoe.

stages.name: Raw Materials
stages.process: Raw rubber sheets, EVA resin pellets, polyester yarn, TPU film, and textile lining are sourced from Tier-2 chemical and textile suppliers. Materials are consolidated and shipped to component factories where they enter the manufacturing process.

stages.name: Component Manufacturing
stages.process: Rubber is compounded with additives, calendered into sheets, and compression-moulded into outsoles. EVA pellets are supercritically infused with nitrogen and moulded into midsole foam. Polyester yarn is circular-knitted into the upper mesh. TPU film is heat-pressed onto reinforcement zones.

stages.name: Cutting
stages.process: Rolls of mesh, lining, and reinforcement are spread on cutting tables. CNC cutting machines process multiple layers at once, following a digital marker to maximise material yield. Roughly 6.7 minutes of labour and machine time per pair.

stages.name: Stitching
stages.process: Cut panels are stitched together — main seams first, then collar and lining. Eyelets and hardware are inserted. Roughly 40–60 individual stitches per shoe. Higher panel counts increase both labour and machine time proportionally.

stages.name: Assembly & Bonding
stages.process: The stitched upper is placed on a shoe last and heated to set its final shape. Adhesive is applied to the midsole edge. Upper and midsole are pressed together in a compression press. The outsole is then bonded in a second pressing stage.

stages.name: Finishing & Quality Control
stages.process: Each shoe is trimmed of excess adhesive, wiped clean, laced, and visually inspected. Random samples from each batch undergo durability, flex, and abrasion testing. Roughly 8 minutes of finishing labour and 3 minutes of QC per pair.

stages.name: Packaging
stages.process: Each pair is tissue-wrapped and placed in a polybag, then in the shoebox with hangtag and inserts. Boxes are labelled with size, SKU, and destination. Pairs are stacked on pallets ready for shipment.

stages.name: Factory Margin
stages.process: The factory's profit on the FOB price. Typically 8–12% for Tier-1 suppliers, 6–9% for Tier-2, and 5–8% for Tier-3. This is what remains after materials, labour, and overheads are covered.
